clinical_documents.title: Pre-authorization Request for Right Knee Arthroscopy - Ava Morales (P-1902)
clinical_documents.content:
To: Harbor Health Medical Review

Re: Ava Morales (DOB: 1984-03-12)  Member ID: HH-88122

We are requesting pre-authorization for right knee arthroscopy with possible meniscal repair/debridement for Ms. Ava Morales. Clinical summary and imaging findings are provided below to support medical necessity.

Clinical history:
- Primary complaint: progressive right knee pain, mechanical symptoms (locking/catching), decreased function.
- Prior treatment: conservative management with NSAIDs (ibuprofen) and physical therapy with inadequate relief.
- Relevant allergies: penicillin.

Imaging summary (MRI right knee, 2026-09-20; Report ID: RPT-010):
- Impression: Complex medial meniscal tear with displaced fragment; unstable tear suspected.
- Findings consistent with a displaced meniscal fragment likely causing mechanical symptoms and joint irritation.

Medical necessity and surgical rationale:
- The MRI demonstrates a complex, displaced medial meniscal tear with an unstable fragment. This imaging finding correlates with the patients mechanical symptoms (locking and catching) and functional limitation despite appropriate conservative therapy.
- Conservative measures have failed to relieve symptoms and the displaced fragment is likely to continue to cause mechanical obstruction and intra-articular damage to articular cartilage if not addressed.
- Arthroscopic intervention (partial meniscectomy and/or meniscal repair as indicated intra-operatively) is indicated to remove or repair the unstable fragment, relieve mechanical symptoms, prevent further chondral injury, and improve function.

Requested procedure(s):
- Right knee arthroscopy with possible meniscal repair or partial meniscectomy (CPT codes: 29881/29882 as applicable).

Provider: Dr. Ana Rivera, Riverside Family Health
Date: 2026-10-30

Attached: MRI report (RPT-010)

If additional information is required, please contact our office at +1-412-555-0199.

clinical_documents.title: Pre-authorization Request for Right Knee Arthroscopy - Ava Morales (P-1902)
clinical_documents.content:
To: Harbor Health Medical Review

Re: Ava Morales (DOB: 1984-03-12)  Member ID: HH-88122

We are requesting pre-authorization for right knee arthroscopy with possible meniscal repair/debridement for Ms. Ava Morales. Clinical summary and imaging findings are provided below to support medical necessity.

Clinical history:
- Primary complaint: progressive right knee pain, mechanical symptoms (locking/catching), decreased function.
- Prior treatment: conservative management with NSAIDs (ibuprofen) and physical therapy with inadequate relief.
- Relevant allergies: penicillin.

Imaging summary (MRI right knee, 2026-09-20; Report ID: RPT-010):
- Impression: Complex medial meniscal tear with displaced fragment; unstable tear suspected.
- Findings consistent with a displaced meniscal fragment likely causing mechanical symptoms and joint irritation.

Medical necessity and surgical rationale:
- The MRI demonstrates a complex, displaced medial meniscal tear with an unstable fragment. This imaging finding correlates with the patients mechanical symptoms (locking and catching) and functional limitation despite appropriate conservative therapy.
- Conservative measures have failed to relieve symptoms and the displaced fragment is likely to continue to cause mechanical obstruction and intra-articular damage to articular cartilage if not addressed.
- Arthroscopic intervention (partial meniscectomy and/or meniscal repair as indicated intra-operatively) is indicated to remove or repair the unstable fragment, relieve mechanical symptoms, prevent further chondral injury, and improve function.

Requested procedure(s):
- Right knee arthroscopy with possible meniscal repair or partial meniscectomy (CPT codes: 29881/29882 as applicable).

Provider: Dr. Ana Rivera, Riverside Family Health
Date: 2026-10-30

Attached: MRI report (RPT-010)

If additional information is required, please contact our office at +1-412-555-0199.
